Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-3{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=-3L\{{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1=-3{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-5=2{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)-1=-3{X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{1}{s+3}.
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)-5=2(\frac{1}{s+3})+{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{5s+17}{(s+3)(s-1)}.
$$

\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2(2s-9)}{(s-1)(s-4)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-2L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-4=2{X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-3=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(s-2){X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)=4 \\ {X}_{1}(s)+(s-3){X}_{2}(s)=3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=3-(s-3){X}_{2}(s).
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-2)[3-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)]+2{X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ 3(s-2)-[(s-2)(s-3)-2]{X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ -({s}^{2}-5s+4){X}_{2}(s) & =4-3(s-2) \\ -(s-1)(s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =-3s+10 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3s-10}{(s-1)(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =3-(s-3){X}_{2}(s) \\  & =3-(s-3)\cdot \frac{3s-10}{(s-1)(s-4)} \\  & =\frac{3(s-1)(s-4)-(s-3)(3s-10)}{(s-1)(s-4)} \\  & =\frac{4s-18}{(s-1)(s-4)} \\  & =\frac{2(2s-9)}{(s-1)(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2(2s-9)}{(s-1)(s-4)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3s-10}{(s-1)(s-4)}.
$$

$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{3}{s-1},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{2}{s-4}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,{e}^{t}+\,\,$ {{field-2}} $\,\,{e}^{4t}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{s-1}\} \\  & =3\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}\} \\  & =3{e}^{1\cdot t} \\  & =3{e}^{t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{2}{s-4}\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}\}-2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & ={e}^{1\cdot t}-2{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & ={e}^{t}-2{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}-2{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{2s}+\frac{7}{2(s-4)}\} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}+\frac{7}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1+\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{2s}-\frac{7}{2(s-4)}\} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}-\frac{7}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot 1-\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$
